items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: Ronnie Zito went to UFA. We were best friends

ctx.x: At Proctor. Ronnie Zito went to UFA. We were best friends and it was like being on opposite sides of the country at that time as a teenager. But I started the music courses, took Rudiments of Music and History of Music and so forth. The rudiments teaches you key signatures and so forth, before theory where you learn harmony and all that. And I got this bug that I wanted to write some arrangements, like Gerry Mulligan’s quartet with no piano. And I did, just by sort in my head solfeggio. And somehow I got some…
Wow, in Little Falls, New York.

items.title: Ronnie Zito interviewed by Monk Rowe & Rick Montalbano, via Zoom, March 9, 2022
items.q: But Jimmy and I used to go to a club called — one of the clubs —

ctx.x: Ronnie, did you study with the drum teacher that Jimmy Wormworth did, Babe something?

No, not Babe Costello, no. It was George Glaskins. That’s who we both studied with. It was great man. I mean he didn’t know anything about jazz or anything like that, or playing a drumset, but he really, rudimentally, he was wonderful you know. And I still think about him, you know, like the way he did things when I went to his lesson you know, we’d have two practice pads set up and he’d — you know he had a beautiful roll man. I’m still working on that. And I think of him all the time.
So there’s a bit of an upstate mystery I’d like to just ask about — there’s Nistico, Romano, Esposito, Mancuso, Zito — like what’s that about?
